extracted.intended_audience: MathML renderer implementers and authors of MathML content (web developers, typesetters)
extracted.subtask_description: Normative rendering, attribute, and authoring rules for MathML presentation elements (mphantom, mfenced, menclose, scripting elements, mmultiscripts, mtable, etc.), intended to guide implementers and authors to achieve correct visual and structural behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: mphantom (Making Sub-Expressions Invisible)
rubrics_metrics.description: The mphantom element renders invisibly, but with the same size and other dimensions, including baseline position, that its contents would have if rendered normally. It accepts a single argument (possibly an inferred mrow).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use mphantom to align parts by invisibly duplicating sub-expressions. It may be wrapped around an mpadded to change size while remaining invisible. Renderers should ensure relative spacing between an mphantom's contents and surrounding MathML elements is the same as if the mphantom were replaced by an mrow with the same content, even across linebreaks. mphantom is not considered space-like unless its content is space-like (affecting operator spacing and grouping rules). mphantom elements accept the common presentation attributes (3.1.9); mathcolor has no effect. When mphantom wraps a subsequence of mrow arguments, default form determination for mo elements inside may change — authors may need to add an explicit form attribute (e.g., form="infix") or wrap each argument in its own mphantom to preserve original form/spacing.

rubrics_metrics.name: mfenced (Expression Inside Pair of Fences)
rubrics_metrics.description: mfenced provides a convenient shorthand to enclose arguments between fences (parentheses/brackets/braces) and optional separators; it is equivalent to an expanded form using mrow and mo elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Renderers that support the recommendation must render mfenced and its expanded mrow-equivalent identically. Default open/close/separators are '(' , ')' and ','; attributes open/close/separators customize delimiters and separator sequence. In RTL contexts mirroring is applied to matching characters. If there are too many separators the extras are ignored; if too few the last separator is repeated; if separators are empty and more than one argument, no separator elements are inserted. Not all fenced expressions can be encoded by mfenced (e.g., embellished separators, mstyle-wrapped fences, missing/extra separators, multi-character separators) — authors may use the expanded form directly. Do not use mfenced with ordinary operator characters (e.g., '+') as separators, since those will be treated as separator elements (mo separator="true") and not as infix operators, changing spacing/semantics.

rubrics_metrics.name: menclose (Enclose Expression Inside Notation)
rubrics_metrics.description: menclose renders its content inside enclosing notation(s) specified by the notation attribute; it accepts a single argument (possibly an inferred mrow).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notation attribute is a whitespace-separated list of values; renderers may ignore values they do not implement but are encouraged to support many. If no notation is given (or empty string), menclose should draw nothing. Multiple notation values are rendered independently (not nested) and may overlap (e.g., 'circle box' draws both). Predefined notations include actuarial, phasorangle, box, roundedbox, circle, left/right/top/bottom lines, various strikes, arrows (recommended names listed), madruwb (Arabic factorial), etc.; phasorangle is directionality-affected. The baseline of menclose is the baseline of its child. Renderers decide paddings (examples suggest ~0.4em horizontal, .5ex vertical).

rubrics_metrics.name: General scripting and limit schemata
rubrics_metrics.description: Presentation scripting elements position scripts around a base (sub/superscripts, overscripts, underscripts, prescripts, tensor indices). Rendering is affected by scriptlevel and displaystyle attributes inherited by expressions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because presentation elements describe abstract notational structure, the base expression in scripting elements (the first argument) must be the entire expression being scripted (e.g., (x+y)^2 should use mrow for the base). There are specialized elements (msub, msup, msubsup, munder, mover, munderover, mmultiscripts) to capture common notation and to position scripts and embellishments in standard locations. Accents vs limits behavior is controlled by accent/accentunder attributes and by movablelimits/displaystyle status for operator bases.

rubrics_metrics.name: msub (Subscript)
rubrics_metrics.description: msub attaches a subscript to a base using <msub> base subscript </msub>.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Within the subscript msb increments scriptlevel by 1 and sets displaystyle to false; base is unchanged. msub accepts the presentation-common attributes. The attribute subscriptshift (length, default automatic) specifies the minimum amount to shift the baseline of the subscript down; default positioning rules are left to the renderer when automatic.

rubrics_metrics.name: msup (Superscript)
rubrics_metrics.description: msup attaches a superscript to a base using <msup> base superscript </msup>.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Within the superscript msup increments scriptlevel by 1 and sets displaystyle to false; base is unchanged. The attribute superscriptshift (length, default automatic) specifies the minimum amount to shift the baseline of the superscript up; default positioning rules are left to the renderer when automatic. Accepts presentation-common attributes.

rubrics_metrics.name: msubsup (Subscript-superscript pair)
rubrics_metrics.description: msubsup attaches both a subscript and a superscript to a base using <msubsup> base subscript superscript </msubsup>.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: msubsup increments scriptlevel by 1 and sets displaystyle to false within both scripts; base is unchanged. Both scripts are positioned tight against the base (contrast with nested scripts which produce staggered positioning). Attributes subscriptshift and superscriptshift (length, default automatic) specify minimum baseline shifts for sub/superscripts; renderers apply their own rules when automatic. Accepts presentation-common attributes.

rubrics_metrics.name: munder (Underscript)
rubrics_metrics.description: munder attaches an accent or limit placed under a base using <munder> base underscript </munder>.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Within underscript, munder always sets displaystyle to false and increments scriptlevel by 1 only when accentunder is false; base is unchanged. If base is an operator with movablelimits=true (or an embellished operator whose mo core has movablelimits=true) and displaystyle=false, underscript is drawn in a subscript position and accentunder is ignored (used for limits on symbols like ∑). Attributes: accentunder (boolean, default automatic) controls accent vs limit; align (left|right|center, default center) controls horizontal alignment of script relative to base. Default accentunder is false unless underscript is an mo element or an embellished operator — in such cases the mo's accent attribute supplies the default. For MathML-Core compatibility accentunder should be set on munder.

rubrics_metrics.name: mover (Overscript)
rubrics_metrics.description: mover attaches an accent or limit placed over a base using <mover> base overscript </mover>.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Within overscript, mover always sets displaystyle to false and increments scriptlevel by 1 only when accent is false; base unchanged. If base is an operator with movablelimits=true and displaystyle=false then overscript is drawn in superscript position and accent is ignored. Attributes: accent (boolean, default automatic) controls accent vs limit; align (left|right|center, default center) controls script alignment. Default accent computed similarly to munder (based on overscript being mo or embellished operator). For MathML-Core compatibility, set accent on mover/munder appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: munderover (Underscript-overscript pair)
rubrics_metrics.description: munderover attaches both underscript and overscript to a base using <munderover> base underscript overscript </munderover>.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: munderover always sets displaystyle to false within both scripts and increments scriptlevel by 1 only when accentunder or accent are false respectively; base unchanged. If base is an operator with movablelimits=true and displaystyle=false, the scripts are drawn in subscript/superscript positions and accent/accentunder are ignored. munderover is used instead of nesting munder and mover so that underscript and overscript are vertically spaced equally and follow the slant of the base. Attributes: accent, accentunder (booleans, default automatic), and align (left|right|center, default center).

rubrics_metrics.name: mmultiscripts and mprescripts (Prescripts and Tensor Indices)
rubrics_metrics.description: mmultiscripts represents base followed by zero or more vertically-aligned (subscript superscript) pairs, optionally followed by mprescripts and prescript pairs; used for presubscripts, postscripts, and tensor notation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: <mmultiscripts> base (sub superscript)* [ <mprescripts/> (presub presup)* ] </mmultiscripts>. Missing scripts must be represented by a valid empty element like <mrow/>. All upper scripts should be baseline-aligned; all lower scripts baseline-aligned. Prescripts (when present) appear after postscripts in the argument sequence. For each script pair horizontal alignment is toward the base (prescripts right-aligned, postscripts left-aligned). The base, scripts, optional mprescripts, and prescripts are all direct children of mmultiscripts; whether an argument is a subscript or superscript is determined by its position (even/odd) ignoring the mprescripts element when counting. The total number of arguments must be odd (no mprescripts) or even (with mprescripts). mprescripts is only allowed as a direct child of mmultiscripts. Attributes: same as msubsup; mmultiscripts increments scriptlevel by 1 and sets displaystyle to false within each argument except base.

rubrics_metrics.name: mtable (Table or Matrix)
rubrics_metrics.description: mtable specifies matrices or tables using mtr rows and mtd cells; rows with fewer columns are effectively padded so each row has the maximum number of columns in the table.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: mtable accepts presentation-common attributes and specialized attributes for fine layout control. MathML does not specify a table layout algorithm — it is the renderer's responsibility to resolve conflicts between width attribute and other constraints (e.g., columnwidth, minimum sizes). Attributes include align (vertical alignment of table relative to environment; may include rownumber), rowalign (vertical alignment of cells within a row), columnalign (horizontal alignment within a column), columnwidth (values: 'auto' | length | 'fit'; default auto) which specifies column sizing rules: auto = as wide as needed; explicit length = fixed width (renderer may wrap/clip contents); fit = share remaining width equally among fit columns (may wrap/clip if insufficient space). When columnwidth is a percentage it is relative to table width. Rules for rowspan/columnspan affect expected number of mtd elements in subsequent rows. Any rules drawn as part of mtable should use mathcolor.
